items.title: Foundation Modernization — Rebrand, Toolchain, OBS Compatibility, and Configuration

items.author: Copilot
items.body:
Addresses foundational tech debt from the `muesli/obs-cli` fork: mismatched identity, incompatibility with OBS 28+ (WebSocket v4 only), outdated CI, and no secret-safe configuration support.

## Rebrand
- Module path: `github.com/muesli/obs-cli` → `github.com/szmyty/obsgod`
- Binary: `obs-cli` → `obsgod`; root command `Use`/`Short` updated
- `.goreleaser.yml`: upstream maintainer/vendor/homepage replaced with project values, schema updated to v2

## OBS WebSocket v5 (goobs v0.8.0 → v1.8.3)
Full API migration across all command files:

| Old | New |
|-----|-----|
| `client.Streaming.*` | `client.Stream.*` |
| `client.Recording.*` | `client.Record.*` |
| `client.StudioMode.*` | `client.Ui.SetStudioModeEnabled()` / `client.Transitions.TriggerStudioModeTransition()` |
| `client.SceneCollections.*` / `client.Profiles.*` | `client.Config.*` |
| `client.ReplayBuffer.*` / `client.VirtualCam.*` | `client.Outputs.*` |
| `client.Sources.GetSpecialSources()` / `ToggleMute()` | `client.Inputs.GetSpecialInputs()` / `ToggleInputMute()` |
| Scene items: name-based properties API | ID-based: `GetSceneItemId` → `GetSceneItemEnabled`/`SetSceneItemEnabled`/`GetSceneItemTransform` |
| Label: `GetTextFreetype2Properties` | `SetInputSettings({"text": ...}, overlay=true)` — works with any text source |

Default port changed `4444` → `4455` (WebSocket v5 default).

## Environment variable support
```sh
export OBS_HOST=192.168.1.100
export OBS_PORT=4455
export OBS_PASSWORD=mysecret
obsgod stream status
```
CLI flags override env defaults. Password no longer needs to appear in shell history.

## CI / toolchain
- Actions: `checkout@v4`, `setup-go@v5`, `golangci-lint-action@v6`, `goreleaser-action@v6`
- Removed `GO111MODULE` env, dropped deprecated linters (`ifshort`, `exportloopref`)
- Lint no longer silences exit code (`--issues-exit-code=0` removed)
- goreleaser: `--rm-dist` / `--skip-publish` replaced with modern `--skip=publish,sign --clean`

Architecture Refactor — Internal Packages, Dependency Injection, and Connection Lifecycle

Summary

Refactor the obsgod codebase to improve maintainability, testability, and extensibility.

The current implementation places all functionality inside a single "main" package and relies on global state for OBS connectivity and configuration.

This issue focuses on internal architecture improvements without changing the external CLI experience.

Goals

1. Introduce Internal Package Structure

Refactor the codebase into logical packages.

Suggested structure:

«cmd/

internal/
├── obs/
├── config/
├── client/
├── commands/
├── output/
└── version/»

The exact structure may differ if a superior organization is identified.

Requirements:

«Reduce responsibility of main.go»

«Move command logic into dedicated packages»

«Isolate OBS-specific code»

«Establish clear package boundaries»

2. Remove Global State

Current implementation relies on global variables for:

«client»

«host»

«port»

«password»

Replace globals with explicit dependencies.

Requirements:

«Pass dependencies through constructors»

«Eliminate package-level mutable state»

«Improve testability»

3. Introduce Configuration Model

Create a central configuration model.

Example:

«type Config struct {
Host string
Port int
Password string
}»

Requirements:

«Single source of truth»

«Shared across commands»

«Compatible with future config-file support»

4. Improve OBS Connection Lifecycle

Current behavior attempts OBS connection during initialization.

This causes commands such as:

«obsgod --help»

to fail when OBS is unavailable.

Requirements:

«Use lazy connection establishment»

«Connect only when required»

«Help and version commands should not require OBS»

«Connection errors should be contextual and actionable»

5. Introduce OBS Service Abstraction

Create an abstraction layer around OBS operations.

Example:

«type OBSClient interface {
StartStream() error
StopStream() error
GetScene() (string, error)
}»

Requirements:

«Decouple commands from websocket implementation»

«Enable future mocking and testing»

«Prepare for future provider architecture»

6. Improve Error Handling

Requirements:

«Centralize common error handling patterns»

«Improve user-facing error messages»

«Preserve CLI usability»

«Avoid duplicated connection and validation logic»

Deliverables

Architecture

«Internal package structure»

«Dependency injection»

«OBS service abstraction»

«Central configuration model»

Code Quality

«Reduced coupling»

«Reduced global state»

«Improved separation of concerns»

Documentation

«Architecture notes»

«Package responsibilities»

«Dependency flow overview»

Acceptance Criteria

«No global mutable OBS state remains»

«Commands function identically from a user perspective»

«Help and version commands work without OBS running»

«OBS connections are established only when needed»

«Internal package structure is documented»

«Architecture is prepared for future provider and workflow systems»

Explicitly Out of Scope

Do not implement:

«Plugin systems»

«Provider systems»

«Stream orchestration workflows»

«Multi-platform streaming»

«New user-facing commands»

These will be addressed in future issues.

Future Direction

This refactor should prepare obsgod for:

«Testing infrastructure»

«Provider architecture»

«StreamGod orchestration layer»

«Workflow automation»

«Multi-platform integrations»
items.title: Architecture Refactor — Internal Packages, Dependency Injection, and Connection Lifecycle

items.author: Copilot
items.body:
This refactor separates CLI wiring, configuration, and OBS integration so the codebase is easier to extend and test without changing the external command surface. It also moves OBS connection establishment to first use, allowing help/version paths to run without a live OBS instance.

- **Architecture**
  - Move command construction out of `main` into `internal/commands`
  - Introduce `internal/config` as the shared connection model
  - Introduce `internal/version` for binary/version metadata
  - Add `docs/architecture.md` to document package responsibilities and dependency flow

- **Dependency injection**
  - Replace package-level mutable OBS/config state with explicit dependencies
  - Build the root command from injected `Config` and OBS service instances
  - Bind persistent flags directly onto the shared config model so command execution sees resolved CLI/env values

- **OBS service boundary**
  - Add `internal/obs.Service` as the abstraction layer for OBS operations
  - Centralize websocket/client lifecycle behind a single service implementation
  - Keep command handlers decoupled from `goobs.Client` internals and request construction

- **Connection lifecycle**
  - Remove eager startup connection behavior
  - Establish the OBS connection lazily on the first command that actually needs it
  - Return contextual connection errors that include the target OBS address

- **Command organization**
  - Rebuild existing command groups (`stream`, `recording`, `scene`, `sceneitem`, `label`, etc.) under the internal command package
  - Preserve the current CLI shape and behavior while eliminating hidden cross-file globals and `init()`-driven registration

- **Focused coverage**
  - Add tests that assert:
    - `--help` does not connect to OBS
    - `--version` does not connect to OBS
    - operational commands trigger a lazy connection attempt and return contextual errors

Example of the new wiring:

```go
cfg := config.Default()
service := obs.NewService(&cfg, version)
cmd := commands.NewRoot(&cfg, service, version)
```

This makes dependency flow explicit:

```text
main -> config + obs service -> commands
```

## Proposed roadmap reconciliation

Milestone 3; parent #46. Role: **preserved broader ledger**.

Broader adapted architecture/governance/ontology scope remains intact; M2 Identity branding is not completion of this migration.

PRs #32, #33 and #34 were merged in order at the owner's explicit request; merged integration is `cc5e5b6b6d4c18c54b1040722924c6b68e5c4ccd`. These do not establish actual Deck6 audio/privacy/session/Kick or successful CI; the billing-lock and missing device acceptance remain open. No release/deployment or issue closure occurred.

New roadmap scope is proposed for owner review, not implementation approval. Existing criteria/dependencies below are retained. [Current proposal](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/master/ROADMAP.md).

## Summary

Bring `obsgod` into the Ego Hygiene documentation/architecture model so the repository has a coherent, durable product definition before the remaining feature work expands.

Use the canonical Ego Hygiene material in `egohygiene/.github` and the reusable baseline patterns in `egohygiene/empathy` as references. Adapt the material to `obsgod`; do **not** blindly copy organization-wide prose that does not apply.

## Goals

Establish a complete architecture and product-documentation layer that explains what `obsgod` is, why it exists, its boundaries, its vocabulary, its design constraints, and how it relates to the future `streamgod` orchestrator.

## Canonical document set to evaluate and adapt

At minimum, review the Ego Hygiene baseline and add the applicable repository-local documents:

- `PURPOSE.md`
- `VISION.md`
- `PRINCIPLES.md`
- `PILLARS.md`
- `FOUNDATIONS.md`
- `ONTOLOGY.md`
- `SYSTEM.md`

Also evaluate the appropriate agent-facing repository instructions (for example `AGENTS.md` and/or `.github/copilot-instructions.md`) so AI-assisted work follows the same architecture and product rules.

## Required architectural content

The resulting documents should explicitly define:

- `obsgod` as the OBS automation/control layer rather than the entire creator runtime
- the intended relationship between `obsgod`, OBS Studio, OBS WebSocket, and future `streamgod`
- CLI → application/service → OBS client dependency flow
- configuration and secret boundaries
- 12-factor-inspired expectations: externalized configuration, stateless command execution where practical, stdout/stderr logging, environment-driven deployment/runtime behavior, and portable binaries
- Steam Deck as a first-class runtime target without coupling the core to SteamOS
- desktop mode and gaming mode as runtime environments rather than separate product architectures
- public library/API boundaries needed for `streamgod` reuse
- terminology for profile, workflow, scene, stream service, recording, replay buffer, OBS instance, provider/platform, and runtime
- what belongs in `obsgod` vs what belongs in `streamgod`
- compatibility/versioning policy
- security model for OBS passwords and platform stream keys
- design principles for non-interactive/automation-friendly operation

## Decision record

Capture the key architectural decisions already made or implied by the current implementation, including:

- modern OBS WebSocket v5 as the supported protocol generation
- Go as the current implementation language
- OBS-specific primitives live in `obsgod`
- creator/platform orchestration belongs above `obsgod`
- `streamgod` should ultimately consume a reusable `obsgod` API/library where practical, with CLI/JSON interoperability as a fallback

Use `DECISIONS.md` or ADRs if that better matches the current Ego Hygiene standard.

## Documentation quality

- Cross-link the documents so they form a navigable knowledge system rather than isolated files.
- Keep README onboarding concise and link into deeper architecture docs.
- Avoid speculative features being presented as implemented behavior; clearly label current, planned, and aspirational capabilities.
- Keep terminology consistent across all documents.

## Acceptance criteria

- The applicable Ego Hygiene architecture/product documents exist in `obsgod` and are customized to this repository.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` contains a current component/dependency view and the intended `streamgod` integration boundary.
- `ONTOLOGY.md` defines the domain vocabulary used throughout the project.
- `ROADMAP.md` distinguishes MVP, production hardening, StreamGod integration, and future expansion.
- `DECISIONS.md` records major architectural choices and rationale.
- Security/secret handling expectations are documented.
- Agent-facing instructions reference the canonical architecture documents.
- README links to the architecture/product documentation without duplicating it.
- No production behavior is changed as part of this issue unless required only to correct documentation that would otherwise be false.

## Roadmap reconciliation (2026-11-11)

**Disposition: broader product backlog, outside the two bounded milestones.**

Broader governance/architecture/ontology/documentation migration. Keep the complete original acceptance in this issue; bounded install/runtime documentation in #8/#22 does not complete this migration.

Roadmap 1: #8 ([milestone](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/1)). Roadmap 2: #23 ([milestone](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/2)). This issue remains open in [Deferred product roadmap — unscheduled](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/3), with its original acceptance criteria intact. This is backlog classification only, without a due date or execution commitment; it is not a prerequisite for Roadmaps 1–2. Scoped overlap is cross-linked rather than counted as completion. Implementation of the new roadmaps awaits owner review.

The supported installer replaces app/plugin while preserving key/settings/media and rollback copies; a separate uninstall is not required.

## Goal and current journey
Install/configure in Desktop Mode, then use OBSGod from Gaming Mode to start a managed background OBS instance, verify capture/output, make a local clip and start/query/stop the configured stream reliably. A running game must not be an artificial prerequisite for OBS lifecycle or control. No-game capture has explicit acceptance in #21.

Standard OBS remains a GUI/rendering application requiring a graphical session; a hidden background window is not a true headless OBS server. Desktop-to-Gaming continuity is not promised without platform evidence.

## Ordered child issues
- [ ] #16 — Reconcile preview provenance and reviewable draft PR boundaries.
- [ ] #10 — Fix OBS startup, WebSocket readiness and Gaming Mode lifecycle.
- [ ] #17 — Authoritative state and automatic panel updates; manual Refresh retained.

## Required behaviors
- Compatible OBS with built-in obs-websocket (OBS 28+), enabled server and matching automatically generated local credentials; successful authenticated readiness is a first-milestone requirement.
- Separate bounded connection/startup budgets, visible startup stages, cancellation and actionable causes rather than an opaque long timeout.
- Separate process, connection, output, pending-operation and game/capture state; live updates work without pressing Refresh.
- Stop disabled only on confirmed idle; Cancel while starting and recovery Stop when output is unknown.
- Coalesce repeated requests and notify on confirmed transitions rather than button presses.
- One keyboard-light installation path for the app and plugin, with accurate Decky detection, optional official interactive bootstrap, preserved settings/media/other plugins and a concrete failure/recovery path.
- Version-aware update checks, verified artifacts, bundled updater, safe idle application and rollback/resume.
- Preserve existing CLI/offline operation, authenticated control, explicit broadcast authorization, isolated profiles, redaction, nonblank output checks and safe paths/recovery.

The historical Desktop-first streaming journey below is reconciled to the current install/configure-in-Desktop, control/test-in-Gaming journey. Session survival remains evidence-driven under #10.

Optional broader workflow/profile/replay-buffer expansion remains in #9/#11; it is not silently marked implemented by this edit. Custom idle content/game transitions and user-facing password controls are deferred to Roadmap 2 (#23). The current generated-password authenticated connection is not deferred.

No legacy acceptance is being declared satisfied: the preserved original issue below documents the earlier planning baseline and scope differences for this review.

## Current baseline and unresolved observations
- master: d0268d13381b463f5950d202917f437a6288a3e4.
- Draft PR #15: 0eb8324c2b1f23fea069570eded1cd0c75d99274.

- Automated Decky installation failed with a generic Big Picture connection hint despite the owner believing Big Picture was closed. This is not proof of its cause.
- OBS absent after switching to Desktop does not prove it never launched in Gaming Mode; the session change may terminate it.
- Native OBS/browser/reference-installer evidence exists; actual Deck/Flatpak/VAAPI/controller/Kick acceptance and current CI receipts are incomplete.

## Open-issue reconciliation
| Existing issue | Disposition |
| --- | --- |
| #8 | Reused as this bounded Roadmap 1 parent; original planning preserved below. |
| #10 | Roadmap 1 runtime/startup/platform child; original capture/performance/session acceptance remains tracked. |
| #7 | Broader governance/architecture-documentation backlog; outside both bounded milestones. |
| #9 | Broader stable reusable API/StreamGod contract; #17's needed state work is a scoped overlap only. |
| #11 | Broader whole-CLI/config/profile/completion polish; diagnostics overlap with this roadmap and password UI with #25. |
| #12 | Broader cross-platform stable-v1/security/supply-chain ledger; #22 is only this campaign's qualification/release subset. |
| #13 | Future separate StreamGod project; not required to fix OBSGod on the Deck. |
| #14 | Post-v1 provider/multistream/creator ecosystem; only the bounded idle concept is separately tracked by #24. |

The six broader issues remain open in [Deferred product roadmap — unscheduled](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/3). This is backlog classification only, without a due date or execution commitment; their original acceptance is preserved, and they are not prerequisites for Roadmaps 1–2.

## Review and closure gates
Owner reviews this roadmap before implementation. During implementation, use small reviewable draft PRs/checkpoints and keep exact revision/command/platform outcomes. Owner review plus full child acceptance precedes merges/closure. Missing required device/CI evidence remains an explicit gate. Close children, this parent and the milestone only when their own acceptance is satisfied. This is not a stable-v1 declaration.

<details>
<summary>Preserved original MVP planning before this roadmap reconciliation</summary>

## Summary

Make `obsgod` useful on a real Steam Deck as soon as possible by delivering a minimal, reliable end-to-end streaming workflow around modern OBS Studio.

The target user journey is deliberately simple:

1. Enter Steam Deck Desktop Mode.
2. Run one `obsgod` workflow command.
3. OBS is launched/connected and prepared automatically.
4. Streaming starts using the configured OBS stream service/profile.
5. The CLI confirms that OBS reports an active stream.
6. The user can then launch/play a game and verify the stream on Kick.

This issue should optimize for getting to the first successful real stream, not for solving every future orchestration problem.

## Requirements

### Steam Deck / OBS runtime detection

- Detect the OBS Flatpak installation (`com.obsproject.Studio`) on SteamOS.
- Detect whether OBS is already running.
- Launch OBS through Flatpak when requested and not already running.
- Wait for OBS WebSocket readiness with a configurable timeout/retry policy instead of relying on a fixed blind sleep.
- Preserve support for non-Steam-Deck Linux/macOS/Windows where practical; Steam Deck-specific behavior should sit behind runtime detection/adapters.

### Diagnostics

Add a first-class diagnostic command such as:

- `obsgod doctor`
- `obsgod status`

Diagnostics should clearly report, where applicable:

- OBS installation detected
- OBS process state
- WebSocket endpoint/authentication state
- OBS version / WebSocket compatibility
- active profile
- active scene collection
- current scene
- streaming state
- recording state
- replay-buffer state
- actionable remediation when a check fails

Support a machine-readable form (`--json`) where feasible.

### MVP workflow

Add a high-level workflow command such as:

- `obsgod workflow start-stream`
- `obsgod workflow stop-stream`

The start workflow should be configurable to:

- launch OBS if necessary
- wait for WebSocket readiness
- select an OBS profile
- select a scene collection
- select an initial scene (for example `Starting Soon`)
- optionally start recording
- optionally start replay buffer
- start streaming
- wait until OBS confirms an active stream
- optionally wait a configurable post-start delay before declaring readiness
- report final state clearly

The stop workflow should safely reverse enabled runtime state and return a useful final status.

### Stream service / secret boundary

Do **not** hardcode Kick-specific logic into the OBS control core.

For the MVP, an OBS profile may already contain the configured Kick ingest/service settings. If generic OBS WebSocket v5 stream-service settings are exposed, design them so secrets can come from environment variables, stdin, or another non-argv secret source. Never print or log stream keys.

Platform-specific orchestration and `KICK_STREAM_KEY` ownership belong primarily in the future `streamgod` layer.

### Automation safety

- Commands must be non-interactive by default or offer a deterministic non-interactive mode.
- Add useful timeouts instead of hanging forever.
- Return meaningful exit codes.
- Handle Ctrl-C / termination cleanly.
- Never leak OBS passwords or stream keys into logs.
- Prefer idempotent behavior (`start` when already started should not corrupt state).
- Consider `--dry-run` for the high-level workflow if it can be implemented cleanly.

## Documentation

Add a focused Steam Deck MVP guide covering:

- installing OBS as a Flatpak
- enabling/configuring OBS WebSocket
- configuring an OBS profile for Kick
- running `obsgod doctor`
- running the one-command workflow
- stopping the stream safely
- common troubleshooting

## Acceptance criteria

- On Steam Deck Desktop Mode, `obsgod doctor` can diagnose a Flatpak OBS installation and WebSocket connection.
- A single high-level `obsgod` command can launch/connect to OBS and start a configured stream without manually clicking through OBS.
- The command waits for real OBS readiness/state rather than using only fixed sleeps.
- Start/stop operations are safe to repeat and have useful exit status/error messages.
- Secrets are not exposed in process arguments, normal output, or logs.
- The workflow can be used with an OBS profile configured for Kick and reaches an OBS-reported streaming state.
- A concise end-to-end Steam Deck test procedure is documented.

## Out of scope

- Full Gaming Mode/background-session hardening
- Twitch/YouTube/multistream provider implementations
- AI clipping/social automation
- The `streamgod` companion CLI itself

Those are tracked separately.

</details>


## Exact candidate and acceptance checkpoint
Qualified local candidate: `0.1.0-deck.5`, source `2287ed4c2f3fcc9b8ec42bbd68ac531063b5d578`; immutable review artifacts `1fbf92ff36eea77bee0f3da186e99d856c80774e`. [Criterion-level packet, PR sequence, downloads and remaining gates](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/86de54abe98614f40287b37b5a33055a515fa501/docs/roadmap1-acceptance.md). [Exact commands/results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/szmyty/obsgod/1fbf92ff36eea77bee0f3da186e99d856c80774e/roadmap1-qualification.json).

Available local checks passed: 56 Go cases (1 optional skipped), 56 Python, 8 Node, vet/vulnerability, typecheck/build/audit, actual-package browsers, repeated package hashes, pinned Decky installer/updater fixtures and real native OBS media/lifecycle. Cross-builds compiled only. Native/protocol fixtures do not establish actual Deck compatibility.

All child acceptance, real Deck/Kick/adoption, working CI and owner review remain required.

No issue is closed from code/package existence. No merge, release/tag publication, deployment, billing change or money spending was performed. Roadmap 2 and the broader deferred backlog remain outside this work.



</details>

## Proposed roadmap reconciliation

Milestone 3; parent #46. Role: **preserved broader ledger**.

Stable reusable API/typed models/JSON/StreamGod contract remain intact; generic provider presets do not complete it.

PRs #32, #33 and #34 were merged in order at the owner's explicit request; merged integration is `cc5e5b6b6d4c18c54b1040722924c6b68e5c4ccd`. Product tree matches the qualified preview6 source plus evidence-only documentation. Fresh merged-tree checks passed:94 Go pass events,70 Python and9 Node. These do not establish actual Deck6 audio/privacy/session/Kick or successful CI; the billing-lock and missing device acceptance remain open. No release/deployment or issue closure occurred.

New roadmap scope is proposed for owner review, not implementation approval. Existing criteria/dependencies below are retained. [Current proposal](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/master/ROADMAP.md).

## Summary

Turn `obsgod` into a clean OBS automation component that can be consumed by the future `streamgod` orchestrator without duplicating WebSocket logic or shelling out unnecessarily.

The CLI should remain useful on its own, but the core OBS capabilities should become reusable through an explicit, stable Go API.

## Goals

### Public automation API

Introduce a reusable package boundary suitable for another repository to import.

The exact package layout may vary, but the result should provide a documented public surface for operations such as:

- connect/disconnect and health checks
- query OBS/runtime status
- profiles
- scene collections
- scenes and scene items
- streaming
- recording
- replay buffer
- virtual camera
- stream-service settings where supported

Avoid exposing transport-library implementation details unnecessarily.

### Context, cancellation, and timeouts

Public operations should support `context.Context` where blocking/network behavior is involved so callers can implement:

- timeouts
- cancellation
- graceful shutdown
- orchestration workflows

### Stable domain types

Define typed domain models for concepts used across the CLI and future `streamgod`, including where useful:

- connection configuration
- runtime status
- stream state
- recording state
- scene/profile identifiers
- workflow result/error information

Avoid passing unstructured maps through the public contract unless the OBS protocol genuinely requires them.

### CLI as a thin adapter

Refactor the CLI so it consumes the same public application/API layer rather than maintaining a parallel implementation.

The goal is:

`CLI -> obsgod application/API -> OBS adapter -> OBS WebSocket`

### Machine-readable interoperability

Even if `streamgod` ultimately imports the Go library directly, preserve a robust process boundary for scripts and other languages:

- `--json` output for high-value read/status commands
- stable exit-code semantics
- no decorative text mixed into JSON output
- stderr for diagnostic/log output

Document this as a supported interoperability contract.

### Workflow/profile primitives

Define reusable primitives needed by an orchestrator without turning `obsgod` itself into a platform-specific creator runtime.

Examples:

- start/stop streaming workflow primitives
- optional recording/replay-buffer toggles
- target profile / collection / scene
- readiness/timeout behavior

If a profile/workflow schema is introduced, make it versionable and clearly distinguish OBS automation configuration from platform credentials.

## Architectural boundary

`obsgod` owns:

- OBS lifecycle/control primitives
- OBS WebSocket integration
- generic OBS state/configuration
- reusable OBS automation workflows

Future `streamgod` owns:

- creator-facing one-shot orchestration
- Kick/Twitch/YouTube provider semantics
- platform stream-key environment variables
- multi-platform policy
- creator workflows that span OBS and external services

Do not blur this boundary merely for convenience.

## Compatibility

- Preserve existing CLI behavior where reasonable.
- Document any intentional breaking API/CLI changes.
- Establish a versioning/deprecation policy for the public package and machine-readable CLI contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- Another Go project can import `obsgod` and start/query/stop OBS streaming without invoking the `obsgod` executable.
- CLI commands use the same underlying application/API implementation.
- Public network operations support cancellation/timeouts.
- Core domain types and errors are documented and testable.
- High-value status operations have stable JSON output and exit-code semantics.
- The `obsgod` vs `streamgod` responsibility boundary is documented in architecture docs.
- No Kick-specific orchestration is embedded in the reusable OBS core.

## Roadmap reconciliation (2026-11-11)

**Disposition: broader product backlog, outside the two bounded milestones.**

Broader stable reusable Go API and StreamGod contract. Roadmap 1 #17 may repair shared state/timeout primitives required for reliability; completing the full public contract remains separate. Roadmap 2 #25 is only managed-instance password/connection UX.

Roadmap 1: #8 ([milestone](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/1)). Roadmap 2: #23 ([milestone](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/2)). This issue remains open in [Deferred product roadmap — unscheduled](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/3), with its original acceptance criteria intact. This is backlog classification only, without a due date or execution commitment; it is not a prerequisite for Roadmaps 1–2. Scoped overlap is cross-linked rather than counted as completion. Implementation of the new roadmaps awaits owner review.

## Summary

Make the Steam Deck runtime story robust beyond the initial Desktop Mode MVP. Validate and support the real lifecycle required to start a stream, move into Gaming Mode, launch a game, and keep OBS/streaming healthy in the background.

This issue is intentionally evidence-driven: first determine what SteamOS actually preserves across Desktop ↔ Gaming Mode transitions, then implement the most reliable supported topology rather than assuming the desktop session survives.

## Investigation

Document and test at least these scenarios on current SteamOS:

1. OBS started in Desktop Mode, then user switches to Gaming Mode.
2. OBS launched directly from Gaming Mode as a non-Steam app.
3. OBS launched/managed by a persistent user-level service or other background mechanism.
4. Game capture under Gamescope/Gaming Mode.
5. Audio capture for game + microphone while Gaming Mode is active.
6. Controller/game performance while streaming.

Record what survives, what terminates, and what capture limitations exist.

## Runtime architecture

Based on the investigation, introduce a Steam Deck runtime adapter or documented launch strategy that can reliably:

- launch OBS in the supported context
- keep OBS available for the required stream lifetime
- establish OBS WebSocket connectivity
- handle restart/reconnect if OBS becomes unavailable
- avoid requiring SteamOS read-only mode to be disabled
- survive normal SteamOS updates as much as possible
- use user-writable/XDG locations for configuration and runtime state

If a user-level service is the best solution, provide a safe install/uninstall flow and document exactly what it manages. Do not require root unless genuinely unavoidable.

## Gaming Mode UX

Provide a workflow optimized for the console-like experience. Depending on what SteamOS permits, this may include:

- start stream in Desktop Mode and receive a clear "safe to switch" readiness signal
- start streaming directly from Gaming Mode
- add a Steam shortcut/non-Steam entry for the streaming launcher
- expose `status`, `stop`, and replay-save actions that can be triggered without returning to Desktop Mode
- document optional controller/back-button/hotkey integrations without hard-coding a specific mapping

## Capture validation

Create a repeatable validation checklist covering:

- video capture of a real game
- expected resolution/FPS
- game audio
- microphone audio
- scene transitions
- recording/replay buffer if enabled
- stream continuity during game launch/exit
- stream recovery after OBS/game failures

Do not claim Gaming Mode support until the workflow is verified against real output.

## Performance / reliability

Measure and document practical Steam Deck defaults for:

- encoder choice
- bitrate
- output resolution
- FPS
- recording/replay-buffer tradeoffs

Keep these as recommended presets, not hard-coded universal assumptions.

## Acceptance criteria

- The repository documents the actual behavior of Desktop → Gaming Mode transitions based on testing.
- A supported architecture exists for keeping OBS/streaming alive while playing in Gaming Mode, or a clearly documented alternative is provided if SteamOS makes that impossible.
- The solution does not depend on disabling SteamOS read-only protection for normal use.
- Game video and audio can be verified on a live/test stream while using Gaming Mode.
- `obsgod` can diagnose/reconnect to the chosen OBS runtime topology.
- A repeatable end-to-end Gaming Mode test checklist exists.
- Known limitations and performance recommendations are documented honestly.

## Out of scope

- Platform-specific creator APIs beyond what is required to validate a stream
- Automated social posting
- AI highlights/clipping
- Broad multi-platform orchestration

</details>

## Proposed roadmap reconciliation

Configure non-secret precedence flags > environment > XDG file > defaults, compatible legacy aliases, profiles/help/completions/JSON; use private secret files/environment references/stdin/keyring where appropriate, never require secret argv. Define config/data/state/cache/runtime and user media paths, safe migration, offline operation and redaction.

New roadmap scope is proposed for owner review, not implementation approval. Existing criteria/dependencies below are retained. [Current proposal](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/master/ROADMAP.md).

## Summary

Polish `obsgod` into a cohesive, automation-friendly CLI product rather than a collection of OBS subcommands.

This issue focuses on ergonomics, configuration, consistency, discoverability, and documentation while preserving the architectural boundary that keeps platform-specific creator orchestration in `streamgod`.

## 12-factor-inspired configuration

Standardize configuration precedence and document it clearly. Prefer a predictable hierarchy such as:

1. explicit CLI flags
2. environment variables
3. XDG configuration file
4. built-in defaults

Use `OBSGOD_*` names for `obsgod`-owned settings.

Requirements:

- XDG-compliant config paths on Linux/SteamOS
- sensible equivalents on macOS/Windows
- no required secrets committed to configuration files
- support environment-variable references for secret values where appropriate
- redact secrets from diagnostics/logging
- deterministic behavior in CI/non-interactive shells

Document the configuration schema and precedence with examples.

## Profiles

Add or formalize reusable OBS automation profiles for common settings/workflows without embedding platform-provider semantics.

A profile may describe concepts such as:

- OBS profile name
- scene collection
- starting scene
- live scene
- recording enabled/disabled
- replay buffer enabled/disabled
- startup/readiness timeout
- optional post-start delay

Profiles should be composable with environment overrides and suitable for future `streamgod` consumption.

## CLI consistency

Audit the full command tree for:

- consistent nouns/verbs
- predictable `get`, `list`, `set`, `start`, `stop`, `toggle`, `status` semantics
- useful aliases only where they improve ergonomics without creating ambiguity
- consistent flags and help text
- examples in `--help`
- meaningful exit codes
- graceful signal handling
- stable behavior when OBS is offline

Add a clear `obsgod version` command and include relevant build metadata without requiring OBS connectivity.

## Output modes

Provide intentional output modes:

- concise human-readable default output
- `--json` for automation/machine consumption
- `--quiet` where useful
- `--verbose` / debug logging without contaminating JSON stdout
- `--no-color` and respect conventional terminal environment behavior

Use stdout for command results and stderr for diagnostics/logs.

## Diagnostics

Polish `doctor`/`status` into a strong support experience:

- explain failed checks rather than only reporting failure
- suggest remediation commands/paths
- distinguish warnings from blockers
- support machine-readable results
- never reveal credentials

## Shell integration

Add supported completion generation/installation for:

- Bash
- Zsh
- Fish

Where practical, add man-page generation or equivalent offline command reference.

## Documentation and examples

Bring docs to product quality:

- quick start
- install/update/uninstall
- configuration reference
- environment-variable reference
- command reference
- Steam Deck quick start
- OBS WebSocket setup
- workflow/profile examples
- shell completions
- scripting/JSON examples
- troubleshooting
- FAQ

Keep README concise and link to deeper docs.

## UX quality bar

- No command should require an active OBS connection merely to display help/version/completions.
- Errors should include context and next steps.
- Secret values should never appear in normal errors, logs, JSON, or examples.
- Commands should be pleasant for both humans and shell automation.
- Avoid unnecessary interactive prompts; when interaction is useful, ensure a non-interactive equivalent exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- Configuration precedence is explicit, tested, and documented.
- XDG-compatible config is supported on SteamOS/Linux.
- Reusable profiles exist and can drive the high-level workflows.
- CLI naming/help/output is internally consistent.
- High-value commands support stable JSON output.
- Bash/Zsh/Fish completions are supported and documented.
- Diagnostics provide actionable remediation without exposing secrets.
- README and docs provide a complete new-user path from installation to first successful OBS command.
- The CLI conforms to the architecture/product principles established in the Ego Hygiene documentation issue.

## Roadmap reconciliation (2026-11-11)

**Disposition: broader product backlog, outside the two bounded milestones.**

Broader whole-CLI/configuration/profiles/completion/documentation polish. Roadmap 1 #17/#18/#19/#22 cover only needed state, diagnostics and supported install guidance; Roadmap 2 #25 covers user-facing WebSocket settings. Preserve this issue's original complete scope.

Roadmap 1: #8 ([milestone](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/1)). Roadmap 2: #23 ([milestone](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/2)). This issue remains open in [Deferred product roadmap — unscheduled](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/3), with its original acceptance criteria intact. This is backlog classification only, without a due date or execution commitment; it is not a prerequisite for Roadmaps 1–2. Scoped overlap is cross-linked rather than counted as completion. Implementation of the new roadmaps awaits owner review.


</details>

## Proposed roadmap reconciliation

Milestone 3; parent #46. Role: **preserved broader ledger**.

Full cross-platform v1 security/release/distribution criteria remain intact; the bounded M2 Deck launch/release subset links here without becoming its full hard dependency.

PRs #32, #33 and #34 were merged in order at the owner's explicit request; merged integration is `cc5e5b6b6d4c18c54b1040722924c6b68e5c4ccd`. Product tree matches the qualified preview6 source plus evidence-only documentation. Fresh merged-tree checks passed:94 Go pass events,70 Python and9 Node. These do not establish actual Deck6 audio/privacy/session/Kick or successful CI; the billing-lock and missing device acceptance remain open. No release/deployment or issue closure occurred.

New roadmap scope is proposed for owner review, not implementation approval. Existing criteria/dependencies below are retained. [Current proposal](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/master/ROADMAP.md).

## Summary

Bring `obsgod` from a polished development tool to a trustworthy v1.0-quality open-source product with comprehensive testing, security controls, reproducible releases, and straightforward installation on supported platforms.

## Testing strategy

Build a layered test suite covering:

### Unit tests

- configuration precedence and validation
- command argument validation
- output formatting / JSON schemas
- workflow state transitions
- error mapping
- pure helpers and domain models

### OBS adapter tests

- mock/fake OBS client behavior
- request/response mapping
- connection failures
- authentication failures
- timeouts/cancellation
- idempotent start/stop behavior

### Integration tests

Create a repeatable integration-test harness for the OBS WebSocket layer where practical. It may use a mock WebSocket server for CI and an opt-in real OBS smoke suite for local/release validation.

### Platform smoke tests

Document and automate what can reasonably be validated for:

- Linux x86_64
- Linux arm64 / Steam Deck class devices
- macOS
- Windows

Do not fake platform support that CI cannot actually validate; document the distinction between built, tested, and community-supported targets.

## Quality gates

Require CI to run appropriate equivalents of:

- `go test ./...`
- race detection where supported
- `go vet`
- `staticcheck` / golangci-lint
- formatting checks
- vulnerability scanning (`govulncheck` or equivalent)
- dependency review on pull requests

Establish a sensible coverage baseline and trend without optimizing for an arbitrary percentage at the expense of useful tests.

## Security hardening

Audit the complete credential lifecycle:

- OBS WebSocket passwords
- generic stream-service secrets
- environment/config loading
- logs and structured output
- crash/error paths
- shell history/process-argument exposure

Add regression tests ensuring secrets are redacted.

Add/refresh:

- `SECURITY.md`
- supported-version policy
- vulnerability reporting instructions
- dependency update automation

Review file permissions for any local state/config containing sensitive material.

## Release engineering

Modernize and validate GoReleaser so tagged releases produce predictable artifacts.

Release artifacts should include appropriate targets such as:

- Linux x86_64
- Linux arm64
- macOS x86_64/arm64 where supported
- Windows x86_64 where supported

Include:

- version/build metadata
- checksums
- changelog/release notes
- license
- reproducible artifact naming

Evaluate and add, where practical:

- SBOM generation
- artifact signing/attestation
- GitHub artifact provenance / supply-chain hardening
- hardened GitHub Actions permissions and dependency pinning consistent with repository policy

## Installation / distribution

Provide a low-friction installation story that does not require modifying an immutable SteamOS root filesystem.

At minimum document/install via downloadable release binary into a user-owned location such as `~/.local/bin`.

Evaluate additional channels based on maintenance cost:

- Homebrew
- Arch/AUR
- `go install`
- package-manager recipes

Do not add a distribution channel that cannot be maintained reliably.

Provide update/uninstall instructions.

## Repository product hygiene

Ensure the repository has current versions of the appropriate project files:

- `LICENSE`
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` where appropriate
- `SECURITY.md`
- `CHANGELOG.md`
- issue/PR templates
- release process documentation

Align these with Ego Hygiene standards where applicable.

## Release readiness audit

Before v1.0, produce a fresh timestamped audit under the repository audit convention that evaluates:

- architecture
- correctness
- tests
- security
- dependencies
- CLI UX
- Steam Deck support
- distribution
- documentation
- supply chain

Convert any remaining release blockers into explicit follow-up issues.

## Acceptance criteria

- CI enforces tests, lint/static analysis, and vulnerability checks.
- Core workflows and configuration have meaningful automated test coverage.
- Secret-redaction behavior is tested.
- Release builds are produced for supported architectures, including Linux arm64.
- Release artifacts include checksums and clear version metadata.
- Steam Deck users can install to user-owned paths without disabling SteamOS read-only protection.
- Security, contributing, changelog, and release documentation are complete.
- A final v1.0 readiness audit identifies no unresolved critical/high release blockers.

## Roadmap reconciliation (2026-11-11)

**Disposition: broader product backlog, outside the two bounded milestones.**

Broader cross-platform stable-v1 quality/security/packaging/supply-chain ledger. Roadmap 1 #19/#20/#22 are the bounded Steam Deck installation/update/qualification subset, not a claim to finish all v1 targets, signing/SBOM/distribution/governance work.

Roadmap 1: #8 ([milestone](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/1)). Roadmap 2: #23 ([milestone](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/2)). This issue remains open in [Deferred product roadmap — unscheduled](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/3), with its original acceptance criteria intact. This is backlog classification only, without a due date or execution commitment; it is not a prerequisite for Roadmaps 1–2. Scoped overlap is cross-linked rather than counted as completion. Implementation of the new roadmaps awaits owner review.

## Proposed roadmap reconciliation

Milestone 3; parent #46. Role: **preserved broader ledger**.

Dedicated StreamGod repository/product boundary requires a new explicit owner decision after organization/name choice; do not create another project or mark this complete from a rebrand.

PRs #32, #33 and #34 were merged in order at the owner's explicit request; merged integration is `cc5e5b6b6d4c18c54b1040722924c6b68e5c4ccd`. Product tree matches the qualified preview6 source plus evidence-only documentation. Fresh merged-tree checks passed:94 Go pass events,70 Python and9 Node. These do not establish actual Deck6 audio/privacy/session/Kick or successful CI; the billing-lock and missing device acceptance remain open. No release/deployment or issue closure occurred.

New roadmap scope is proposed for owner review, not implementation approval. Existing criteria/dependencies below are retained. [Current proposal](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/master/ROADMAP.md).

## Summary

Track the creation of the future `streamgod` companion project that sits above `obsgod` and delivers the actual creator-facing one-shot experience.

This issue lives in `obsgod` until a dedicated `streamgod` repository exists. When implementation begins, create/migrate the work to the appropriate repository while keeping `obsgod` focused on generic OBS automation.

## Product goal

The primary user experience should eventually be as simple as:

- `streamgod start`
- `streamgod status`
- `streamgod stop`

On a Steam Deck, `streamgod start` should be able to prepare OBS, configure the selected streaming provider securely, start the desired OBS workflow, verify readiness, and tell the user when it is safe to play/switch modes.

## Architecture

Preferred dependency direction:

`streamgod -> obsgod public API -> OBS Studio / OBS WebSocket`

A subprocess/JSON fallback may be supported for portability, but do not duplicate OBS protocol logic inside `streamgod`.

`streamgod` owns creator/platform orchestration. `obsgod` remains the reusable OBS control layer.

## MVP provider: Kick

Implement Kick first, behind a provider abstraction that does not force future Twitch/YouTube behavior into the same concrete implementation.

Configuration should support environment-driven secrets, for example:

- `KICK_STREAM_KEY`
- platform/channel metadata as needed
- OBS credentials through the established `obsgod` configuration contract

Never require the Kick stream key to be supplied as a command-line argument. Never print it, persist it accidentally, or include it in crash/log output.

## 12-factor-inspired runtime

Design the companion CLI around:

- externalized configuration
- environment-backed secrets
- deterministic/non-interactive execution
- logs/events to stdout/stderr with machine-readable mode
- minimal hidden mutable state
- portable configuration via XDG paths on Linux/SteamOS
- graceful shutdown and explicit lifecycle commands

A config file may define non-secret defaults/profile selection while secrets remain externally supplied.

## `streamgod start` MVP

A successful start should be able to orchestrate the equivalent of:

1. load/validate configuration
2. run preflight diagnostics
3. launch/connect to OBS through `obsgod`
4. select the desired OBS profile / collection / starting scene
5. configure the provider/stream service securely if needed
6. optionally start recording
7. optionally enable replay buffer
8. start streaming
9. wait for OBS to report an active stream
10. apply a configurable ingest/readiness delay if needed
11. optionally transition from `Starting Soon` to `Live`
12. print a concise readiness result such as "LIVE — safe to launch/switch to Gaming Mode"

The operation should be idempotent and should fail safely with actionable diagnostics.

## `streamgod stop` MVP

Stop should safely:

- transition to an ending scene if configured
- stop streaming
- stop recording/replay behavior according to profile policy
- preserve useful recordings/clips
- optionally leave OBS running or stop it based on configuration
- report final state

## Profiles

Support simple creator profiles, initially something like `gaming`, that compose provider-independent workflow behavior with provider configuration.

Profiles should be able to express concepts such as:

- provider
- OBS profile
- scene collection
- starting/live/ending scenes
- recording policy
- replay-buffer policy
- readiness delay
- OBS lifecycle policy

Keep credentials out of committed profile files.

## Steam Deck experience

Integrate with the validated Steam Deck runtime from `obsgod` so the ideal flow is eventually:

1. invoke `streamgod start` from Desktop Mode or Gaming Mode
2. receive a confirmed LIVE/readiness state
3. launch/play a game in Gaming Mode
4. stream continues in the background
5. `streamgod status` and `streamgod stop` remain accessible with minimal friction

Optionally support a Steam non-game shortcut / controller-friendly launcher once the underlying lifecycle is stable.

## Extensibility

Design provider and workflow boundaries so future work can add, without rewriting the core:

- Twitch
- YouTube
- Restream/multistream providers
- metadata/category/title updates
- chat/dashboard launchers
- clip/highlight pipelines
- external creator automations

Do not implement those integrations in the MVP unless required to prove the abstraction.

## Acceptance criteria

- A dedicated `streamgod` repository/project is established when implementation begins.
- `streamgod` consumes `obsgod` rather than duplicating OBS WebSocket logic.
- `streamgod start`, `status`, and `stop` exist with deterministic automation-friendly behavior.
- Kick is supported as the first provider.
- `KICK_STREAM_KEY` or equivalent secret configuration never needs to appear in argv or committed config.
- A gaming profile can start OBS/streaming with one command and report confirmed readiness.
- The workflow is documented and tested on Steam Deck.
- The architecture allows additional providers without coupling them to the OBS core.

## Out of scope for the initial MVP

- AI highlight detection
- automated social posting
- creator analytics
- plugin marketplace
- complex cloud orchestration
- broad multi-platform implementation beyond establishing the provider boundary

The first objective is simple: one command, then play.

## Roadmap reconciliation (2026-11-11)

**Disposition: broader product backlog, outside the two bounded milestones.**

Future separate StreamGod companion repository/project. The current campaign fixes this OBSGod repository; creating or changing another repository is not required. Basic managed OBS controls stay in #8; #24's idle views do not establish the complete StreamGod orchestration product.

Roadmap 1: #8 ([milestone](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/1)). Roadmap 2: #23 ([milestone](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/2)). This issue remains open in [Deferred product roadmap — unscheduled](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/3), with its original acceptance criteria intact. This is backlog classification only, without a due date or execution commitment; it is not a prerequisite for Roadmaps 1–2. Scoped overlap is cross-linked rather than counted as completion. Implementation of the new roadmaps awaits owner review.

## Proposed roadmap reconciliation

Milestone 3; parent #46. Role: **preserved broader ledger**.

Preserve full provider/multistream/creator/content ecosystem acceptance; M2 basic RTMP presets are only a subset and M3 new parent does not replace/narrow this ledger.

PRs #32, #33 and #34 were merged in order at the owner's explicit request; merged integration is `cc5e5b6b6d4c18c54b1040722924c6b68e5c4ccd`. Product tree matches the qualified preview6 source plus evidence-only documentation. Fresh merged-tree checks passed:94 Go pass events,70 Python and9 Node. These do not establish actual Deck6 audio/privacy/session/Kick or successful CI; the billing-lock and missing device acceptance remain open. No release/deployment or issue closure occurred.

New roadmap scope is proposed for owner review, not implementation approval. Existing criteria/dependencies below are retained. [Current proposal](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/master/ROADMAP.md).

## Summary

Capture the post-MVP expansion path so the original creator-runtime vision is not lost after `obsgod` and the initial `streamgod` workflow become stable.

This is an umbrella roadmap issue, not a requirement for the first `obsgod` v1.0 release. Most implementation should ultimately live in the future `streamgod` repository or dedicated integrations rather than expanding the generic OBS core indiscriminately.

## Provider expansion

After Kick is proven, evaluate provider adapters for:

- Twitch
- YouTube Live
- Restream or other multistream routing
- additional platforms only where APIs/terms and maintenance burden make sense

Provider adapters should own platform-specific concepts such as stream credentials, titles/categories, channel URLs, API authentication, and metadata updates.

`obsgod` should continue to expose generic OBS stream-service capabilities rather than accumulating platform-specific business logic.

## Multi-platform orchestration

Design StreamGod-level policy for:

- one provider vs multiple providers
- direct OBS output vs restream service
- provider-specific readiness/health
- partial failure behavior
- start/stop ordering
- platform metadata synchronization
- credential isolation

Do not assume simultaneous direct outputs are always the correct architecture; evaluate OBS/plugin/restream tradeoffs first.

## Creator workflows

Potential optional modules/integrations:

- Starting Soon / Live / BRB / Ending scene workflows
- chat/dashboard launchers
- Discord presence/notifications
- music/now-playing overlays
- replay/clip tagging
- local archive organization
- post-stream metadata and summaries

Keep the core workflow deterministic and make integrations opt-in.

## Content pipeline

Explore a modular post-stream pipeline for:

- recording/replay ingestion
- highlight/clip extraction
- vertical/social crops
- subtitles/transcripts
- export presets for TikTok/Shorts/Reels
- optional AI-assisted highlight suggestions

This should integrate with existing creator tooling rather than forcing media processing into `obsgod` itself.

## Extension model

Before adding many integrations, define the smallest maintainable extension contract. Evaluate:

- provider interfaces
- workflow hooks/events
- subprocess/plugin contracts
- configuration namespaces
- capability discovery

Prefer boring, explicit interfaces over a premature plugin marketplace/runtime.

## Observability

For multi-service workflows, consider structured lifecycle events such as:

- preflight
- OBS ready
- provider configured
- stream starting
- stream live
- scene changed
- recording/replay active
- provider degraded
- stopping
- stopped

These events should support human output and machine-readable automation without leaking credentials.

## Acceptance criteria

This umbrella can be considered complete when:

- Kick MVP has validated the provider abstraction.
- At least one additional provider can be added without modifying OBS core architecture.
- Multi-platform strategy and failure semantics are documented before implementation.
- Creator integrations are modular/optional rather than coupled to basic streaming.
- The content/clip pipeline has a clear boundary from OBS control.
- Follow-up implementation work has been moved into focused issues in the appropriate repository(s).

## Not a v1 blocker

Do not delay a reliable Steam Deck + Kick MVP or `obsgod` v1.0 for these features. Reliability and the one-command core experience come first.

## Roadmap reconciliation (2026-11-11)

**Disposition: broader product backlog, outside the two bounded milestones.**

Post-v1 provider/multistream/creator/content ecosystem. Keep its full future scope outside both bounded milestones. Roadmap 2 #24 only implements the separately agreed local idle-content/game-transition subset; it does not import provider expansion or the ecosystem.

Roadmap 1: #8 ([milestone](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/1)). Roadmap 2: #23 ([milestone](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/2)). This issue remains open in [Deferred product roadmap — unscheduled](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/milestone/3), with its original acceptance criteria intact. This is backlog classification only, without a due date or execution commitment; it is not a prerequisite for Roadmaps 1–2. Scoped overlap is cross-linked rather than counted as completion. Adds the Desktop setup → Gaming Mode streaming preview: private local URL/key setup, isolated OBS Flatpak settings, rendered-game capture checks, local test clips and Decky controls with truthful output status. Start requires nonblank frames and advancing output bytes; Stop confirms inactive output. Microphone defaults off; credentials stay in private files/stdin.

A persistent diagnostic console beneath Refresh status retains 100 whitelisted events, polls progress during operations, pages/clears history and exports every retained page through Copy console log. Exports include UTC timestamps, severity and version, excluding settings/URLs/keys/raw subprocess errors. Clipboard fallback preserves focus and reports failure truthfully.

The one-click updater now replaces both the app and OBSGod plugin from a Desktop launcher or shell script. It validates the bundle and pinned release download, checks output is safely stopped before closing managed OBS, checks/installs missing user Flatpaks, privately backs up preferences/key and runs the existing staged app installer. A separate, unprivileged Go helper uses Decky's authenticated local request/confirmation routes for exactly the verified unprivileged OBSGod ZIP, verifies the enabled installed version and restores only OBSGod's plugin-order position. It never directly deletes root-owned plugin files or unrelated plugins. Unconfirmed output/active recording blocks unsafe shutdown; partial installation is reported accurately and can be retried. Existing settings/key/media/OBS files and previous release directories are preserved. Decky Loader itself remains a prerequisite.

**Milestone 3 streaming implementation prepared for review (2026-11-13).** The owner authorized #47/#24/#48/#49/#50 and explicitly excluded #51. [Owner packet](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/codex/m3-output-confirmation/docs/m3-review.md) · [Criterion ledger](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/9ad051ecbb41df92c723a54bdfb6aaaeb1097898/criteria.json) · [Install guide](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/codex/m3-output-confirmation/docs/candidate-8-install.md).

**This issue remains open.** Actual Steam Deck/SteamOS/OBS33/Flatpak/Gamescope/AMD/controller/provider/adoption and degraded-device/performance criteria remain unrun; required human review is pending; fresh CI executed zero steps because of the account billing lock. Native OBS30.2.3 and fixture browsers do not supply device proof. No source merges, issue closures, releases, deployments, Store submission, transfer or spending occurred. Preserve every original criterion/dependency below; earlier proposal-only status is historical and superseded only for these five authorized features. Broader #7/#9/#12/#13/#14 and excluded #51 keep parent #46 open.

---

**Next milestone proposal after M2 source merges:** the owner requested the next-push list, not M3 implementation yet. Recommended first visible feature batch: **#47 stream/profile editor + #24 custom idle/BRB media**, then #48 audio/session resilience, #49 recording/replay/clips, #50 stream health and #51 one validated optional paid offer. Keep broader #7/#9/#12/#13/#14 ledgers separately bounded, with no automatic companion repository.

M2 actual Deck/provider/adoption, CI, final identity and release/site decisions remain carryover gates; they are not silently completed by source merges. This priority list does not create new hard dependencies. Wallet activation is optional/deferred.

---

**Proposed for owner review.** This issue prepares a later implementation scope; creating it does not approve the plan or establish completion. Preserve existing acceptance and explicit output/secret/data safety. No migration, account creation, release, deployment, store contact/submission or spending is performed by this planning issue.

## Scope

After a supported M2 launch, use actual successful-user/support observations to prioritize deeper configuration and sustainable optional revenue. Preserve #24's rich image/video/scene acceptance and the original broader #7/#9/#12/#13/#14 ledgers. Do not pretend a Deck launch completes a whole creator ecosystem or a cross-built binary establishes platform support.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Review and prioritize bounded advanced profiles, audio/runtime resilience, replay/recording/clips, stream health and one validated paid-offer experiment.
- [ ] Reconcile and complete or explicitly disposition every original linked ledger; no acceptance disappears when scope is reclassified.
- [ ] Keep local core/Stop/recovery/security/accessibility/offline use available; optional services/assets respect rights/privacy and actual channel policy.
- [ ] Require exact source/review/device/provider evidence for each claimed capability, and explicit authorization for other repositories, paid services, releases and deployments.
- [ ] Measure actual user value, support/operating costs and voluntary/paid uptake rather than promising revenue.

## Dependencies and boundaries

No new hard dependency is imposed on independent qualification or repair.

Related existing work: #7, #9, #12, #13, #14, #24. Preserve those issues' complete original criteria; this bounded work does not close broader ledgers.

## Owner/external gates

M3 is proposed and independently reviewed. The dedicated StreamGod project in #13 requires an explicit owner boundary decision, not automatic creation or silent completion.

## Proposed children and preserved ledgers

- [ ] #47 — Add an easy advanced stream and profile editor
- [ ] #24 — Add custom idle banner/video and game-aware scene transitions
- [ ] #48 — Improve live audio-device, capture and runtime resilience
- [ ] #49 — Add recording, replay-buffer and local clip workflows
- [ ] #50 — Expose stream health and measured quality recommendations
- [ ] #51 — Validate one sustainable optional paid offering before building it
- [ ] #9 — Define the reusable obsgod API and StreamGod integration contract
- [ ] #12 — Production hardening and v1.0 release readiness — tests, security, packaging, and supply chain
- [ ] #13 — Bootstrap the StreamGod companion CLI — one-command Kick streaming on Steam Deck
- [ ] #14 — Post-v1 roadmap — multi-platform providers, multistream, and creator automation ecosystem
- [ ] #7 — Adopt Ego Hygiene architecture, ontology, governance, and product documentation

**Research delivered:** all14 current research criteria are complete through [the two-journey brief](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/6f7edf957db630f7662254decbac18aae73a870a/docs/research-51.md), [official-policy findings](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/6f7edf957db630f7662254decbac18aae73a870a/docs/store-policy-research.md), [40 pinned sources](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/6f7edf957db630f7662254decbac18aae73a870a/docs/research-51-sources.json), and [criterion mapping](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/6f7edf957db630f7662254decbac18aae73a870a/docs/research-51-criteria.json). Recommendations and owner questions remain distinct from owner adoption or any implementation/external outcome.

**Owner-rescoped on 2026-11-13.** This issue tracks two research journeys for Decky Stream. The owner now explicitly authorizes changing #51 from a paid-offer implementation proposal into research. Each journey produces an evidence-backed recommendation; choosing no monetization or direct-only distribution is a valid result.

## Journey 1 — Monetization research

Explore whether any sustainable monetization fits the product and its users.

- [x] Identify actual user problems, available demand/willingness-to-pay evidence and gaps in that evidence; distinguish observations from hypotheses.
- [x] Compare voluntary support, plausible optional paid offerings and keeping the product entirely free. Avoid selecting a product, price, provider or account before the evidence supports it.
- [x] Assess ownership/licensing, applicable channel rules, support capacity, operating costs and the value an offer would deliver.
- [x] Record a recommendation: pursue, defer or do not monetize, with alternatives, assumptions, tradeoffs and precise owner decisions.
- [x] If an experiment is recommended, outline a small separately reviewable experiment and its success/stop criteria, costs and required approvals.

## Journey 2 — Decky Store eligibility and distribution research

Determine whether and how this project could be distributed through the Decky Store, using truthful source and asset provenance.

- [x] Pin current official policies, submission templates, licensing/asset rules, technical/native-build requirements, testing requirements and support-link/monetization rules.
- [x] Compare the actual project's AI-assisted development history, sources, assets and build layout with those requirements. Document clear requirements, ambiguities and concrete blockers.
- [x] Assess legitimate available paths and the changes/evidence each would require. Prepare any necessary maintainer questions for owner review before contact.
- [x] Compare Store distribution with verified direct downloads, including installation/update friction, maintenance burden and user trust.
- [x] Record a recommendation and evidence: viable path, clarification needed, deferred or direct-only, plus the exact next actions and owner/external decisions. An accepted Store listing is an external outcome rather than a condition for closing the research.

## Shared research deliverables and completion

- [x] Keep the two journeys separately readable, with dated sources, findings, alternatives, uncertainty and recommendations.
- [x] Preserve a free local core, offline operation, explicit stream controls, privacy and accessibility in every proposed path.
- [x] Separate completed research from any proposed implementation, payment/account setup, release, deployment or Store submission.
- [x] Give the owner a concise decision checklist. Research completion does not require launching a paid offering, receiving money or obtaining Store acceptance.

## Boundaries and roadmap

Parent: #46. Milestone 3.

This research is independent of completing and qualifying the streaming plugin. Remaining implementation/acceptance is retained in #46 with the intact original criteria and dependencies.

Related work: #37 (Store policy/disposition), #42 (optional support), #45 (distribution/adoption), #12 and #14. Preserve and link their existing evidence during later consolidation.

External contact, another-repository submission, account/payment changes, spending, releases and deployments retain their existing owner-authorization gates. Prepare concrete proposals before those actions.

<details>
<summary>Original paid-offer proposal and future implementation gates — retained history</summary>

The owner has replaced the original delivery scope with the two research journeys above. The original criteria below remain available as historical context and possible future implementation gates; they are not additional requirements to launch a paid product before completing this research.

**Proposed for owner review.** This issue prepares a later implementation scope; creating it does not approve the plan or establish completion. Preserve existing acceptance and explicit output/secret/data safety. No migration, account creation, release, deployment, store contact/submission or spending is performed by this planning issue.

## Scope

Use repeat-user demand and support-cost evidence to choose one optional offer: for example original licensed asset packs, bounded setup/support services or a separately hosted service with clear ongoing value. No provider, price, infrastructure or account is selected by this proposal. A free support button alone does not prove a subscription market.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record real customer problem/willingness-to-pay observations, ownership/rights, capacity, cost assumptions and a go/no-go decision.
- [ ] Verify applicable Decky/channel paid-feature rules and truthful provenance; core/accessibility paywalls are not assumed acceptable and store admission is never guaranteed.
- [ ] Prepare exact owner-approved pricing/payment/refund/support/privacy/availability terms and per-unit operating costs before purchasing infrastructure or taking money.
- [ ] Keep the free local core and sensitive stream data independent; no hidden telemetry or required cloud account for existing operation.
- [ ] Launch only with required approvals, then measure actual net receipts, user outcomes and support costs; do not guarantee income or disguise an unbuilt service as ready.

## Dependencies and boundaries

No new hard dependency is imposed on independent qualification or repair.

Related existing work: #12, #14. Preserve those issues' complete original criteria; this bounded work does not close broader ledgers.

## Owner/external gates

Payment/vendor choice, account setup, money movement, paid resources, new repositories and deployment/release require concrete owner authorization. Do not contact maintainers or submit a paid integration without authorization.

## Roadmap

Parent: #46. Milestone 3; proposed scope for owner review.


</details>

items.author: szmyty
items.body:
## Shared tooling reference

[Realm PR #64](https://github.com/egohygiene/realm/pull/64) contains a reviewable local act installer, explicit validation runner and managed-cloud proxy/CA helper. [Reflector PR #266](https://github.com/egohygiene/reflector/pull/266) is the qualified consumer example. These are draft source candidates, not published prerequisites: this issue can begin with the directly installed pinned act client and this repository's own test commands. Inspect and explicitly select any candidate source before reusing it.

## Outcome

Make the repository's available GitHub Actions tests reproducible in a Codex cloud workspace with `nektos/act`, execute the complete locally supportable validation matrix, and repair reproducible failures through reviewable changes. Retain clear evidence for jobs that require native platforms, real Steam Deck hardware, GitHub services, or credentials.

This is the handoff for a separate implementation agent. Related acceptance: #12 (hardening), #22 (qualification), and #46 (Milestone 3). It does not replace their remaining criteria.

## Verified starting point

Inspected default `master` at `ed7d100d356ce803d2cb1c1afef3836759deef10`. No root `AGENTS.md` or `.actrc` was present. Refresh live state before execution: the M3 work has separate draft PRs #58–#60 and may change before this issue starts. Read `CONTINUITY.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, applicable scoped instructions, and `docs/steam-deck-qualification.md`; coordinate with existing source work.

Current workflow inventory:

| Workflow | Local coverage to establish |
| --- | --- |
| `.github/workflows/build.yml` / `build` | Go build/tests; run the Linux matrix member in act. macOS/Windows require native evidence; a Linux container with those labels is not equivalent. |
| `coverage.yml` / `coverage` | Go race and coverage checks. |
| `lint.yml` / `golangci` | golangci-lint, including its PR/new-issues mode and tool compatibility. |
| `goreleaser.yml` / `goreleaser` | Existing snapshot build with `--skip=publish,sign`; retain the non-publishing boundary. |
| `docs-preview.yml` / `build-preview` | Shared metadata, offline site build, Python site checks, and local artifact retention. |
| `steam-deck.yml` / `candidate` | Go race/vet/vulnerability, Python installer/backend tests, Node typecheck/tests/build/audit, reproducible packaging, Playwright, and nested-Docker native OBS/capture fixtures. |

Current declared tools include Go toolchain `1.27.4` (`go.mod` language version `1.23.0`), Node `24.19.0`, npm `11.9.0`, Python `3.12`, Playwright `1.62.0`, and govulncheck `v1.9.0`. Workflow selectors such as `^1`, `latest`, and golangci's action version need reconciliation against those exact source inputs, not guessed downgrades. The current candidate packaging workflow names `0.1.0-deck.7`; preserve historical package/evidence identities and reconcile the version only through the selected current source.

## Implementation and execution

1. Inventory the exact selected revision, workflow events/jobs/matrices, test scripts, required tools, permissions, network inputs and external side effects. Check current open PRs and avoid duplicating or overwriting the M3 stack.
2. Install a reviewed pinned act binary and verify its published checksum. Provide Docker daemon/socket access, adequate disk, the cloud proxy/CA inside runner containers, and digest-pinned compatible Ubuntu runner mappings. Read the cloud runtime's Docker instructions. Reuse the shared act/.actrc work if available; its release is not an invented prerequisite to a documented standalone local setup.
3. Add an inspected repository `.actrc` and one documented local entry point for humans and agents. Explain configuration precedence and keep tokens, secrets, personal paths and machine-specific sockets outside tracked defaults. Include job listing/dry-run, event fixtures and ignored local artifacts.
4. Run each safe Linux job through act individually first, then the appropriate combined validation. Example selectors, to validate against the installed act version and actual workflow inventory:

       act -l -W .github/workflows
       act push -W .github/workflows/build.yml -j build --matrix os:ubuntu-latest
       act push -W .github/workflows/coverage.yml -j coverage
       act push -W .github/workflows/lint.yml -j golangci
       act push -W .github/workflows/goreleaser.yml -j goreleaser
       act workflow_dispatch -W .github/workflows/docs-preview.yml -j build-preview
       act workflow_dispatch -W .github/workflows/steam-deck.yml -j candidate

   The commands require the reviewed runner/configuration first; their presence here is not a passing execution claim. Exercise pull-request-specific behavior using a reviewed synthetic event where relevant.
5. Work through genuine workflow/test failures with bounded fixes and focused regression checks, rerunning the affected jobs at the new exact revision. Preserve test strength, production gates and source semantics. Report environment setup failures separately from product defects.
6. Address artifact upload/download through act's local artifact service when compatible, or retain verified outputs locally and explicitly record that GitHub artifact delivery was untested. Nested Docker needs daemon-visible workspace mounts, proxy/CA trust and suitable user permissions; validate this actual path rather than assuming host and runner paths match.
7. For an unsupported step, execute its repository-owned test command directly when meaningful. Preserve its result as fallback evidence, with the reason the act step is partial/unavailable. Do not globally mark tests successful by skipping jobs or disabling checks.
8. Keep a workflow/job/test coverage ledger: exact revision, act/runner digest/tool versions, event/matrix, command, exit result, counts and explicit skips, reviewed log/artifact paths or hashes, fixes, and remaining next actions. Use passed/failed/partial/unavailable/not-applicable distinctly.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A fresh cloud workspace can reproduce setup, list jobs and execute the documented supported act entry points.
- [ ] Every existing workflow job/matrix member is accounted for; locally supported tests run, and unsupported portions have specific reasons and meaningful fallback results where possible.
- [ ] Go, Python, Node, security/static checks, packaging/reproducibility, browser tests and available native Linux OBS fixtures are included according to the selected source.
- [ ] Reproducible defects are fixed in reviewable changes or linked to scoped follow-ups with a concrete next step; no blanket claim of all tests passing hides skips.
- [ ] A second run proves the retained commands and fixes against the recorded final source.
- [ ] Sanitized evidence, limitations, source changes and refreshed continuation instructions are ready for owner review.

## Boundaries and handoff

Use local execution only for this task; do not dispatch hosted Actions, publish releases/packages/sites, stream to real providers, change protection/billing settings, or alter immutable review artifacts. Use synthetic credentials and local fixtures where possible; never publish stream keys, OBS passwords, private profiles or unreviewed logs. Any genuinely required secret must be supplied through the workspace's supported secret mechanism.

Native macOS/Windows, actual Deck/Flatpak/Gamescope/hardware/performance/controller checks, public provider-viewer verification, GitHub OIDC/hosted runner behavior and production publication remain separate evidence. Act success does not close those existing acceptance gates.

Deliver a bounded draft PR or stack with the coverage/failure ledger and exact reproducible commands. Preserve active work and leave merges, publication and unrelated milestone implementation for their own authorization.

items.author: szmyty
items.body:
**Qualified repair:** PRs #69–#72 are merged; actual repair qualification is exact source `4699235e9e925b76ca492d5a00a375ed37fb338e`, with [criterion-level proof](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/6f7edf957db630f7662254decbac18aae73a870a/audits/qualification-4699235.md) and [immutable review evidence](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/tree/eb92598f3a4a0dc426749c290bacfe7251452909). The original reproduction/recovery below is retained as history.

A fresh-output local ACT run leaves generated frontend assets unusable by the normal checkout owner. This was reproduced during the audit in #67; the six ACT jobs themselves passed. This is a developer-workflow defect, separate from the remaining hosted/device gates in #46. Closed #61 is provenance.

### Reproduction and evidence

Exact clean source: `cf12abe6c620dcbea3b806d1aa63a4715adea26a`, tree `d24d5435af64400da8bb665714b908cbbe638f7c`.
Linux x86_64 host UID/GID1000, Node24.19.0/npm11.9.0, ACT0.2.97; Ubuntu24 runner digest `19619a010b204f44c5340bff7d39b68551109fe6a56a53f75201ea91e05d4270`.

1. Start with the generated, ignored `steamdeck/decky/dist` absent, as on a fresh checkout. The audit verified no tracked paths, preserved the existing output and recorded its ownership/hashes.
2. Run the supported local candidate job (the actual reproduction used the full repeat six-job sequence):
   ```sh
   python3 scripts/local-ci.py candidate --act /workspace/.obsgod-tools/pkg/bin/act --state /workspace/.obsgod-tools/completion/act
   ```
3. ACT recreates `steamdeck/decky/dist` as UID/GID0, mode0755. Four JavaScript outputs are UID0/mode0644; the license file is UID1000. The checkout parent remains UID1000/mode0700.
4. As the normal UID1000 owner, run:
   ```sh
   npm --prefix steamdeck/decky run build
   ```
   Actual exit1:
   ```text
   Error: EACCES: permission denied, open 'dist/decky-api.js'
   at .../steamdeck/decky/rollup.config.js:15:1
   ```

Observed 2026-11-13T23:31:22.554027+00:00; failure-log SHA256 `42135c973f91e058d1f9ad30cd86d97f7b587a7d1990c242ae5c1614dae17ea4`. Source stayed clean/unchanged. The full ownership inventory, completed ACT receipts and failure/recovery logs are retained in the [audit packet](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/d6f67159fb88e664a4dad2e57950c29c0407653f/audits/local-act-2026-11-13.md) at evidence-only commit `d6f67159fb88e664a4dad2e57950c29c0407653f`.

### Expected behavior

A documented ACT run should leave generated frontend outputs usable by the ordinary checkout owner, including when the generated directory initially does not exist.

### Safe recovery observed

An attempted cross-parent move of the root-owned directory failed with EACCES without changing files. A same-parent rename to the absent, already-ignored `steamdeck/decky/.local-ci` preserved the exact output; a new UID1000 build then passed. No sudo/chown/chmod was used. All14 root candidate/audit hashes stayed unchanged. This is a bounded recovery workaround, not a fix.

### Acceptance

- [x] ACT followed by normal-host frontend typecheck/test/build passes from both initially absent and reused generated output, without manual privileged repair or renaming.
- [x] Preserve actual execution identities/provenance; choose bounded build identity or output isolation rather than recursively changing checkout ownership.
- [x] If cleanup is needed, verify safe non-symlink generated paths and preserve existing outputs; refuse unsafe/foreign paths.
- [x] Preserve production root guards and the nonroot installer/browser fixtures.
- [x] Retain exact repaired revision, ACT/host commands, ownership before/after, raw results and source/artifact-preservation evidence.

No duplicate billing, Dependency graph, physical Deck, provider, or publication scope is added here.
